title: SSE duplicate/ordering anomalies causing customer-facing partial outputs — investigation & mitigation playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Over the past 48 hours we received multiple customer escalations where hosted API SSE streams returned duplicated or out-of-order tokens and, in some cases, truncated final outputs that the client perceived as partial responses. Customers include a mid-market chat app (customer A) and an enterprise workflow automation vendor (customer B) on Dedicated. Symptoms observed: duplicate token sequences, short reversed token fragments near reconnects, streams that close with HTTP 200 but missing terminal token, and clients re-requesting the same prompt and seeing different completions. Impact crosses Hosted/Dedicated/Private: different surface but same failure mode (edge proxy reconnect + worker handoff). This ticket captures the investigation findings, immediate mitigations deployed, and a repeatable playbook for future escalations.
steps_to_reproduce: Start a long-running SSE generation (>= 8k tokens simulated sequence) via the hosted API with streaming enabled.
Introduce a mid-stream proxy socket interruption (TCP FIN followed by quick reconnect) or simulate worker-side preemption during KV flush.
Observe client receiving a reconnect and a resumed stream: check for duplicate tokens and ordering anomalies in the token sequence IDs emitted by the runtime.
Replay across Dedicated with autoscaler-triggered drain to reproduce worker handoff ordering differences (customer B environment).
If present, collect request_id, session_id, edge-proxy logs, and worker logs; correlate token sequence numbers and KV cache checkpoint timestamps.
acceptance_criteria: Server-side sequence monotonicity filter prevents duplicate tokens from being emitted to clients for retried/resumed sessions.
New telemetry dashboard shows per-session duplicate rate, median reorder span, and percent of sessions with truncated final token within 1h of rollout.
SDK/Console guidance updated with explicit resume semantics and recommended client-side final-token validation marker.
Canary customers (2 hosted + 1 dedicated) see zero regressions for 72 hours after soft rollout; playbook validated by on-call and SRE.
recent_updates: 2026-03-01: Triage call (on-call, SRE, runtime, product) — initial theory: race between edge proxy reconnect handling and worker checkpoint replay. Assigned Lucas Rivera as lead.

2026-03-03: Dumped correlated traces for 7 affected sessions from customer A — identified pattern: edge ACKs accepted before worker KV checkpoint was durable, worker replayed from older offset on reconnect leading to duplicate tokens.
2026-03-05: Implemented emergency sequence filter (runtime) that drops tokens with sequence_id <= last_delivered_seq for a session. Deployed as hotfix in hosted canary (region us-west-2).
2026-03-07: Hotfix reduced duplication incidents for canary customers from 0.9% of streams to 0.02%. Metrics dashboard (Link below) created.
2026-03-09: Created SDK marker PR to emit explicit final-token boundary event and to surface server-provided resume_token to clients (github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482).
2026-03-12: Roadmap established for medium-term durable session journaling + improved reconnect handshake; initiated dedicated-customer patch that pins sessions to capacity during critical streams.
mitigation_and_next_steps: Short-term (hotfix): Keep sequence monotonicity filter for 72-hour canary; enable per-tenant stricter buffering for affected customers.
Short-term (observability): Add alert: session_duplicate_rate > 0.1% over 15m triggers P1 to on-call. Added field duplicate_count to existing request logs.
Medium-term: Implement durable per-session journal (append-only event log) that guarantees at-least-once replay with idempotent emission semantics. Target: runtime-1.25.
Medium-term: Add an explicit resume handshake: client provides last_seen_seq and server responds with resume_token + last_server_seq; server refuses to resume if mismatch without backfill request.

Customer remediation: For escalated customers, offer data collection window + optional on-demand backfill of missing output via short-term non-streaming response, and provide a temporary config to pin to Dedicated capacity.
Testing: Create fuzz harness simulating TCP FIN/RESET, worker preemption, and proxy buffering under multiple real-world patterns; add to CI regression suite.
Postmortem: Draft full incident writeup and share in #incidents and Confluence. Schedule blameless RCA meeting with stakeholders.
notes_for_support: When contacting customers: request full request_id and session_id, set log_level=debug and collect edge+worker traces for window +/-30s from last client-observed token.

Suggested customer message: 'We're actively investigating a streaming ordering issue. As a short-term workaround, please retry the request or enable non-streaming backfill in the Console for affected runs. We'll notify you once the canary is green.'
If customer reports truncated final token, offer immediate backfill of final full output via non-streaming endpoint and escalate to SRE for session pinning.
